findings.problem: Step 3 leaves the highest-impact decision in the whole task ambiguous: 'decide whether this correctness fix warrants bumping the sentinel to v3 ... recommend bumping to v3 given the file's own precedent comment' — this is advisory phrasing ('decide', 'recommend'), not a mandate. Two reasonable weak models will diverge: one bumps `versionGroupBackfillKey` to a v3 sentinel (forcing every existing deployment to re-run the backfill once under the wider bounds), the other leaves the sentinel alone (the bound fix then only helps *future* book IDs written after this deploy; already-existing letter-leading books, if any, silently stay unindexed forever since the one-time gate is already tripped). This is a real behavioral fork with a prod-data consequence (whether stale deployments self-heal), not cosmetic — it needs to be a mandate either way.
